https://www.cei.int/ansa/178469.text: Vilnius will summon Russian representative on damage sustained at the embassy in Kyiv (ANSA) - TRIESTE, AUG 2 - The Lithuanian Foreign Ministry will summon the Russian representative in Vilnius after the Lithuanian embassy building in Kyiv was damaged in a massive Russian attack. Lithuanian Foreign Minister Kęstutis Budris reported on X that "missiles struck just meters from the Embassy" and that "fortunately, our staff did not suffer." "Russia's campaign of terror against Ukraine continues without limits. There is no sign of any genuine willingness to stop it, to seek peace or engage in negotiations" he stated, adding "The Kremlin's objective remains the same: destruction, death and intimidation. The response is clear: increase pressure on Russia through stronger sanctions and step up support for Ukraine." (ANSA). Know-how Exchange Programme Call for Proposals 2026 now open! https://wsbt.com/news/local/warsaw-hosts.text: Zimmer Biomet Center Lake Pavilion in Warsaw hosted its 9th HireKosciusko Hiring Fair on Thursday. The event allowed for those looking for jobs to meet up directly with employers face to face. 14 different companies were represented at the hiring fair, as well as higher education opportunities such as Grace College, Ivy Tech, and WorkOne Northern Indiana. Allyn Decker from OrhoWorx believes that this event helps people get through the job searching process better. "For anybody who's been in a job search recently, it can be discouraging when everything is requiring online applications," said Decker. Decker also spoke about how not going through an online application process can keep a candidate from getting automatically eliminated due to AI screening. Around 120 job seekers were expected to come to the event.

https://www.politico.eu/article/starlink.text: KYIV — Ukrainian interceptors still cannot use the internet at high speed to shoot down Russian attack drones or conduct mid-strike operations as of Friday morning, Ukrainian officials and a drone operator said, despite U.S. President Donald Trump saying SpaceX founder Elon Musk had lifted speed restrictions on his Starshield service. “Morning tests show the speed limits of 140–160 km/h are still there, and the navigation isn’t working properly,” a Ukrainian government official told POLITICO on condition of anonymity. “As of this morning, instances of connectivity loss at speeds of 161 km/h are still being observed. There is currently no confirmation that the restrictions have been lifted,” a defense ministry official told reporters on Friday. Advertisement Advertisement Ukrainian drone units started testing speed limits from Thursday evening, shortly after Trump told reporters that Musk had restored Starlink. While some tests recorded speeds of up to 200 km/h over the Black Sea and noted an improvement, the drones still rapidly lost signal once flying above the 160 km/h speed limit. “So, the key point is: We accelerate above 180 km/h, fly for a couple of minutes, the connection drops. It falls to 140–150 km/h and then is re-established — but the situation is better,” a drone pilot from Ukraine’s top drone unit known as Magyar’s Birds told POLITICO. “So it works better, but with constant connection interruptions,” the pilot, whose call sign is Leon, said. The speed limit on Starshield, Starlink’s service designed for military purposes, stalled key operations and partially disabled crucial drone interceptors against Russian Shaheds attack drones. Musk said that the U.S. government controlled Starshield, while U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the administration could not direct SpaceX or Musk regarding restrictions or slowdowns of Starlink services in Ukraine as it is a private company. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy argued the Starlink restriction was a planned operation to specifically restrict Starshield’s operating speed over Ukraine. The Ukrainian government said that it was not told why that had happened for days. However, the Wall Street Journal reported Thursday that Trump had called Musk and asked him to lift restrictions. “I don’t want to say. That’s a very interesting situation. My relationship with Elon is very good. I don’t want to comment on it, whether I called, or someone else called … The bottom line: he put it back,” Trump told reporters on Thursday evening.
